about: Discussion prompts for the debrief. 'game' prompts always show; the others show when that question set was used. Teachers: edit freely.
game: Citizens: when did you feel most watched? What did you change about how you moved?
Did anyone pass a page to a stranger? What made you decide whom to trust?
Ruler: which rule did the most to keep order? Which hurt innocent people most?
Look at the wall at the start and at the end. Who noticed the changes, and when?
How many innocent people were taken? Was that a cost the ruler counted?
1984: Winston's job is to change the record. How did amending the wall today compare?
The Party watches through telescreens. How did knowing where the cameras were change what you did?
Julia breaks rules in small ways to survive. Did anyone play like Julia? Like Winston?
Why might a state want people to doubt their own memory of the rules?
Animal Farm: The commandments on the barn wall change, and the animals doubt their memories. How did the wall in this game work the same way?
Squealer explains every change. What would a Squealer have said about today's amendments?
Boxer trusts and works harder. Did trust protect anyone in this game?
Which rule today would the pigs have liked best, and why?
Civics: Which rules today would break the First Amendment? Which would break the Fourth?
The ruler could take anyone the cameras saw. What does due process add that this game lacked?
Changing a rule and punishing people who broke the old wording: why does the Constitution forbid ex post facto laws?
What checks on the ruler's power would have changed today's outcome?
